title: Run a small read on the isolate that asked for it
impact: Moonshot: challenged the assumption that every read has to cross an isolate boundary. Exps 264, 258 and 239 each closed a candidate against a `round-trip floor` nobody had priced, and exps 209/239 attacked it by amortising the hop across several queries — both rejected because a shared reply cannot complete independently. This removes the hop for one query instead of sharing it, which neither rejection covers. `ReaderPool.select` runs a statement on the calling isolate when the per-SQL high-water mark exps 260/264 already keep says it has never returned more than 64 rows and the pool has watched it twice; `Database.open` opens one reader connection past the pool and reserves it, because a worker's slot is marked free before the worker's `finally` releases its connection and the connections are NOMUTEX. A row cap in `decodeQuery` throws, resets the abandoned statement — which would otherwise hold that connection's read transaction open and serve every later read a stale snapshot — and hands the query back to a worker; any inline failure falls back the same way and reports nothing, which is free of consequence because reader connections are READONLY. Two collections of four alternating-order lane-isolated AOT passes, `ab_drift_check` REPRODUCED on every primary: a 6-column point read -74.8% (8.4 -> 2.1 us) and a 21-column one -71.0% — flat in projection width, unlike exp 264, because what is removed is per-request; a 20-row page -35.7%; and a point read issued while four 1,000-row reads hold the whole pool -94.9%, because the hop's cost is also the queue in front of it. The guard lane written to kill it did the opposite: eight distinct point reads issued together run four-wide across the pool today and strictly serially inline, and serial is 70% faster, because four workers cannot make up a per-request overhead larger than the request. Both controls return more rows than the cap admits, so they run identical code and read +0.1% / +3.2%. Costs are bounded and measured: the first execution that outruns the cap pays +24.7%, once per statement because the high-water mark rises with it; peak RSS rises by one SQLite connection (+0.1 to +1.7 MB); and the main isolate gives up ~2 us per point read and at most ~16 us per admitted read. That last is a positioning trade rather than a measurement, so the PR is held for human review; `RESQLITE_INLINE_ROW_MAX=0` restores the previous behaviour exactly.
